title: major gulf bourses mixed amid escalating middle east conflict 2026 09 09
text:
Sept 9 (Reuters) - Most Gulf stock markets closed lower on Wednesday as the intensifying Middle East conflict and mounting energy security risks weighed ​on investor sentiment.
The conflict escalated sharply after Iran-backed Houthi forces launched strikes across ‌several Saudi cities, setting key oil installations ablaze and drawing a crucial U.S. ally deeper into hostilities.
The confrontation worsened after U.S. forces struck multiple Iranian oil tankers, triggering retaliatory attacks on commercial vessels and a ​U.S. military base in Jordan.
The multi-front escalation poses a severe threat to ​regional energy output and critical trade arteries. The attacks directly jeopardize crude ⁠transit through the Red Sea — a vital alternative route that has become increasingly ​strained as flows through the crucial Strait of Hormuz remain nearly blocked.
Saudi Arabia's benchmark index (.TASI)
, opens new tab
 fell 0.2%, hit ​by a 1.7% drop in the country's biggest lender by assets Saudi National Bank (1180.SE)
, opens new tab
.
Brent crude futures were up $2.77, or 2.83%, at $100.69 a barrel by 1033 GMT.
Banks including Goldman Sachs and Bank of America raised ​their oil price forecasts citing tightening supplies as crude rallied to multi-week highs.
Dubai's ​main share index (.DFMGI)
, opens new tab
 was down 0.3%, dragged down by a 1.8% slide in top lender Emirates NBD (ENBD.DU)
, opens new tab
.
Fresh ‌geopolitical ⁠flare-ups continue to fuel regional caution, as persistent tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, maritime bottlenecks, and tit-for-tat strikes keep energy supply risks elevated, said Joseph Dahrieh, managing director at Tickmill.
"Attention remains focused on the Oman-Iran waterway management agreement and its implications ​for maritime security," Dahrieh ​said.
Looking ahead, Dahrieh emphasized ⁠that geopolitical volatility will remain the primary headwind for GCC equities —capping sentiment during escalations, while any tangible de-escalation could unlock a ​rebound. Nonetheless, resilient domestic fundamentals are expected to provide a crucial ​buffer, limiting ⁠broader downside risks.
In Abu Dhabi, the index (.FTFADGI)
, opens new tab
 advanced 0.9%.
The Qatari index (.QSI)
, opens new tab
 eased 0.1%, with petrochemical maker Industries Qatar (IQCD.QA)
, opens new tab
 retreating 1.9%.
Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index (.EGX30)
, opens new tab
 gained 0.6%.
